question: A 55-year-old diabetic patient requires amputation for a gangrenous right foot with ischaemia extending to the mid-calf. The vascular surgeon confirms that blood supply is adequate at the tibial tubercle level but not below. Which amputation level offers the BEST functional rehabilitation outcome, and why?

answers.text: Below-knee (transtibial) amputation at the tibial tubercle level — preserves the knee joint, enabling prosthetic gait with near-normal energy expenditure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Preserving the knee joint is the most important determinant of prosthetic walking success. Transtibial amputees require only ~10–40% more energy to walk than non-amputees; transfemoral amputees require 60–100% more. If vascular status permits a viable BK stump, it should be chosen.

answers.text: Above-knee (transfemoral) amputation at mid-thigh — safer margin above the ischaemia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: If the blood supply is adequate at tibial tubercle level, selecting a higher amputation sacrifices the knee joint unnecessarily. Transfemoral amputation doubles the energy cost of prosthetic gait and dramatically reduces community ambulation rates in diabetic elderly patients.

answers.text: Syme's amputation (ankle disarticulation) — preserves maximal limb length

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: If ischaemia extends to mid-calf and blood supply is only confirmed at tibial tubercle level, a Syme's amputation would heal poorly in ischaemic tissue. The answer must respect the vascular watershed confirmed by the surgeon.

answers.text: Hip disarticulation — eliminates all risk of stump infection in a diabetic patient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hip disarticulation is reserved for proximal vascular failure or tumour — it is not justified by distal ischaemia with adequate flow at the tibial tubercle. It would result in the worst possible functional outcome and is not indicated here.

overallFeedback.feedback: The cardinal rule of amputation level selection: preserve the most distal viable level. Knee preservation (BK amputation) reduces prosthetic energy cost by 50–60% compared with AK amputation and dramatically improves community ambulation. Always choose the lowest level with viable blood supply.
Excellent. The knee joint is the most important functional lever in lower-limb prosthetics — preserve it whenever the vascular supply permits a viable below-knee stump.
